summary: Convert a BASIC program to assembler source
description: Converts a BASIC program to readable assembler source that runs as a machine program. Each BASIC line becomes a section with the original as a comment and the label L<line>. Besides the .asm file, a line map (JSON) is created for the debugger.
The converter picks the smallest stage the program needs: 1 = integer, 2 = floating point, 3 = strings. --stage sets the upper limit.

options.help: Target system. Sets the start address, processor and BASIC dialect. The MEGA65 has no floating point (E331).
Read the source as Turbo BASIC XL (target atari8 only, otherwise E344). Blocks like WHILE/WEND and PROC/EXEC become jumps.
Folder with the hardware database (data). With --runtime embed, also the source of the runtime.
options.default_text: VC_DATA or next to the program

options.help: Highest allowed stage. The smallest one the program needs is chosen. Numbers other than 1 to 3 report E300.
Include the floating-point runtime even if the program does not need it.
Translate / as integer division. Otherwise it needs stage 2.
compact: each operation calls a runtime routine. inline: simple integer expressions appear as direct 6502 instructions (longer in the source, shorter in the runtime).
include: the runtime comes from data/sys via #include. embed: it is copied into the result file, which can then be assembled without an include folder.
Do not keep a line number at run time: smaller, but error messages have no line.
Do not take lines that consist only of REM.
Output file with the assembler source.
Line map: BASIC line, source line and label in the assembler.
Only check and report the stage and number of lines. No files are written.

examples.title: Turbo BASIC XL with a stage limit

notes: Commands the converter does not translate (OPEN, LOAD, LIST, NEW ...) are reported (E311), not silently replaced. On the Atari, you always get the note I150 about numbers.
You can print the syntax tree with vcc basic ast.
